person.occupation: Seaman, Politician, Colonial Wool Merchant, Colonial Secretary

note.p: John MacArthur likely met Godwin while awaiting colonial court martial in England for political dissent in Australia. Born in Devon in 1767, MacArthur was ensigned in the English navy before being stationed in Australia where he would become one of the most significant Australian wool merchants and subsequently a figurehead within early Australian politics. Notably, he was a leading figure in the Rum Rebellion military coup against Governor Bligh in 1808 which resulted in two years of army control, and held office as Colonial Secretary within this period. Financially, he rose as Australia’s most prominent wool refiner and merchant. The supply of wool to England proved highly profitable and would become a hallmark of early imperial trade. At the time of his death in 1834 he owned 24,000 acres of land valued at £300,000.
